summary: Turrell V. Wylie (1927–1984) was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Sinology who earned his B.A. degrees at the University of Washington and studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche. He later served as Associate Professor and Professor at the University of Washington.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Tyler Dewar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and under traditional teachers Tashi Wangchuk, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche.
Tyler M. Richard works in Indology and linguistics. He held a post in South Asian Studies at Harvard University and was attested as a faculty member at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

Tyler Williams is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held posts at Columbia University, Australian National University, and the University of Chicago, where he served as Assistant Professor.

Tzungkuen Wen specializes in Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Queensland under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He served as Lecturer at Fuyan Buddhist Institute and Head of Counseling and Guidance Center at Chung-Hwa Institute.
U-tain Wongsathit works in Indology and linguistics. He held a Ph.D. in Sanskrit post at Silpakorn University in 2003 and earned a Ph.D. in Sanskrit from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 2010.

U. Ghimire works in Indology and philosophy. After health degrees from Purbanchal University and Southeast University, Ghimire earned a PhD from Nepal Sanskrit University in 2023, having held positions at Chitwan Hospital, Rambadevi College, Global Health Alliance, and Nepal's government.

U. V. Swaminatha Iyer (1855–1942) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Meenakshisundaram Pillai and held posts at Pachaiyappa's College (around 1903–1919) and Annamalai University (around 1932–1935).

Linguist Udaya Narayana Singh studied at the University of Calcutta and University of Delhi (Ph.D.). He held posts at Baroda, South Gujarat, Delhi, Hyderabad, Visva-Bharati, Amity University, and served as Director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages.

Udo Posch (1922–1965) studied Tibetology and linguistics at the University of Vienna under Robert Bleichsteiner and Herbert W. Duda. He later served as Lecturer at the University of Graz and held a post at the University of Washington.
Ugyen Pelgen works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ujjwal Kumar specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University. He served as Assistant Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2006–2016) and became Professor at the University of Calcutta in 2016.

Ulrich Mammitzsch (1935–1990) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Halle, Hamburg, SIU Carbondale, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (Ph.D.), later serving as director of East Asian Studies at Western Washington University.

Ulrich Pagel works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and was appointed Seiyi Kiriyama Professor in Buddhist Studies at SOAS University of London in 1999.

Ulrich Schneider (1922–1992) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig, the University of Freiburg, and the University of Münster.

Ulrich Timme Kragh specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, having studied at Copenhagen and Karmapa International Buddhist Institute. He held posts at Copenhagen, Harvard, Geumgang University, IIAS, Sydney, the Australian National University, and Apabhramsha Sahitya Academy.

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff (1848–1931) studied at Bonn and Berlin under Johannes Schmidt, Otto Jahn, and Moriz Haupt. In linguistics, history, and archaeology, he held professorships at Greifswald, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Berlin.
Ulrike Niklas works in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Klaus Ludwig Janert and held a post at the University of Cologne.

Ulrike Roesler studied at the University of Münster (PhD) and works in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She taught at Marburg and Freiburg, and held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Wolfson College, and the University of Oxford.
